questions.q: Calculate the net radiation heat flux exchange between two bodies with surface temperatures of $120°\text{C}$ and $25°\text{C}$. The radiation heat transfer coefficient is $7.0\text{ W/m}^2\text{·K}$.

A pipe with a 4 cm inside diameter and 12 cm outer diameter is insulated with asbestos ($k = 0.54\text{ W/m·K}$). The inside wall temperature of the pipe is maintained at $500°\text{C}$ while the outside surface of the asbestos is at $90°\text{C}$. Calculate the heat loss per meter length.

A 5 m thick flat plane ($k = 60\text{ W/m·K}$) is well insulated on its sides, while the top and bottom surfaces are maintained at $150°\text{C}$ and $80°\text{C}$, respectively. Assuming steady-state heat conduction, calculate the temperature 4 m below the top surface.

A solid sphere of diameter $D = 0.5\text{ m}$ and surface emissivity of 0.8 contains electronics that dissipate 100 W of heat. If it does not receive radiation from the surroundings, what is the surface temperature?
In heat transfer by conduction, due to symmetry the heat flow at a point is perpendicular to the isothermal surface through the point. This mode of conduction is a characteristic of:
The heat transferred radially across an insulated pipe per unit area:
options: Inversely proportional to the thermal conductivity
Decreases from pipe wall to insulated surface
Increases from pipe wall to insulated surface
questions.answer: Decreases from pipe wall to insulated surface

questions.q: If a man touches two metals which were kept together at room temperature, why would one metal feel colder than the other?
options: One has a high temperature coefficient
One has a high thermal conductivity
questions.answer: One has a high thermal conductivity

Which of the following statements is not a key feature of Fourier's heat conduction?
options: It defines an important material property called thermal conductance
It is a vector expression indicating that the heat flux is normal and in the direction of decreasing temperature
